items: Alkanes with up to four carbon atoms are colourless, odourless gases; pentane to heptadecane (C5 to C17) are colourless, odourless liquids; the higher members from C18 onwards are waxy solids, also colourless and odourless.
Alkanes are non-polar or very weakly polar, insoluble in polar solvents such as water but soluble in non-polar solvents such as hexane, benzene and ether.

Their physical constants (boiling point, melting point, density) increase with the number of carbon atoms, whereas solubility decreases with increasing molecular mass. Branched-chain alkanes boil lower than their isomeric straight-chain alkanes: butane boils at -0.5 degrees C and 2-methylpropane (isobutane) at -11.7 degrees C.

blocks.prompt: Why do branched alkanes have lower boiling points than straight-chain alkanes (Quick Check 11.2a)?
blocks.explanation: Alkane molecules are held together only by weak intermolecular forces that depend on how much surface the molecules can bring into contact. A straight chain can lie alongside its neighbours over its whole length; a branched isomer is more compact and nearly spherical, so less surface touches, the forces are weaker and less energy is needed to boil it.
